Direction checked for inversion and found correct. For F fibrewise O(4)+O(5) the maximal destabilizing subsheaf is the slope-5 line subbundle, so 0 -> L_5 -> F -> L_4 -> 0 is the HN filtration as written. Dualizing gives 0 -> L_4^vee -> F^vee -> L_5^vee -> 0, so after tensoring by the line bundle O_{P(E^vee)}(2)|_C the degree-20 W_4 is the SUB and the degree-16 W_5 the QUOTIENT — exactly as claimed. No sub/quotient inversion, and the degree bookkeeping is consistent with CLM-Z-DEG. Extension-class placement also checks: fibrewise Ext^1(O(4),O(5)) = H^1(P^1,O(1)) = 0, so no local obstruction is visible, and the global class sits in H^1(B, p_*O(1)) via the Leray/local-to-global sequence with R^1p_*O(1)=0 — matching FND-0097. The refusal to assume a global split is therefore substantive, not cosmetic.

Conclusion true, stated justification false; confirmed only after repair. The attempt writes 'Because Gamma is finite over the base, both pi_* and restriction to Gamma are exact on this filtration.' Finiteness of Gamma over the base gives exactness of (-)|_Gamma (a SES of vector bundles is locally split, so it survives ⊗ O_Gamma) and exactness of pushforward along the finite map Gamma -> B. It says nothing about exactness of pi_* along the curve fibration on 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0, which is only left exact. Surjectivity pi_*W ->> pi_*W_5 requires R^1 pi_* W_4 = 0, which holds because deg W_4 = 20 > 2g-2 = 10 — a vanishing the attempt never states. Likewise coker(phi_4) = 0 requires H^1(W_4(-Gamma)) = 0, i.e. deg 20-6 = 14 > 10, plus commutation of the cokernel with base change and Nakayama to pass from geometric fibres to the sheaf. With those two degree vanishings inserted the snake lemma applies and coker phi ≅ coker phi_5 as modules; since Fit_0 depends only on the isomorphism class of a finitely presented module, Fit_0(coker phi) = Fit_0(coker phi_5) follows. Clause (1) therefore stands, but only on grounds the attempt does not give. Recorded as a finding candidate because FND-0097 contains the same misstatement.

Charged against theorem clause (3). Three independent grounds. (a) Self-contradiction between statement and status: CLM-Z-SCHEME carries status 'gap' and GAP-Z-SCHEME-CMP is recorded at HIGH severity, yet clause (3) asserts flatly that Z^{bal}_{ev} 'equals Z^{bal}_{AJ}'. The parenthetical '(residual base-relative writeup gap recorded)' is an admission, not a hypothesis; it does not conditionalize the assertion. A weakest-sufficient lemma must either conditionalize the clause or move it to the exclusion list, and this one does neither. (b) The right-hand side is undefined: Z^{bal}_{AJ} is introduced only as 'the Abel–Jacobi incidence of O_C(Gamma) ≅ L', with no scheme structure specified anywhere in the statement or in Step 4. An equality 'as closed subschemes' whose right-hand side has no declared scheme structure is not a determinate assertion, so clause (3) cannot be certified either way. This produces a dilemma the attempt never confronts: if Z^{bal}_{AJ} is defined as the scheme-theoretic fibre b^{-1}(e) of the twisted AJ morphism b: Div^6 -> Pic^0, Gamma |-> L(-Gamma), then clause (3) follows almost formally from FND-0096 together with two standard facts (Fit_0 commutes with arbitrary base change, and R^1 pi_* commutes with arbitrary base change in relative dimension 1), and the clause carries far less content than its presentation suggests; if Z^{bal}_{AJ} is meant to carry any other structure, clause (3) is simply unproved. (c) The one genuinely non-formal ingredient is stack-theoretic, not editorial: the identification of N = L(-Gamma) with a pullback of a Poincare bundle requires a Poincare bundle for C/B^{bal}, whose universal curve has no section and whose base is an algebraic stack, so the object exists a priori only up to a G_m-gerbe / Brauer twist. Fit_0 is insensitive to twisting the module by a line bundle from the base, so this is very likely repairable, but it is mathematical content of exactly the stack-versus-scheme kind, and describing it as a 'writeup gap' understates it.

FND-0096 is adjudicated with the hypothesis 'Gamma a relative Cartier divisor finite etale of degree n over the base'. The universal degree-6 divisor over Div^6_{C/B} is finite flat but etale only over the reduced-support open. The attempt invokes FND-0096 over all of Div^6 — that is, precisely including the non-reduced divisors where clause (3)'s scheme-theoretic content is not already forced by the geometric-point statement (2). The underlying determinantal computation plausibly extends to finite flat Gamma (the rank count h^0 = g+n-1, kernel H^0(omega) of dimension g, cokernel H^1(omega) of dimension 1, and the perfect Serre pairing as intrinsic derivative do not use etaleness), but the attempt neither notes the hypothesis mismatch nor supplies the extension. Second, unaddressed direction mismatch: FND-0096 fixes Gamma and varies the base over Pic^0, whereas the needed statement fixes W_5 and varies Gamma over Div^6. Converting one into the other is a base-change/pullback argument along the Abel–Jacobi morphism; it is available, but it is never written, and Step 4's phrase 'After translating the CE evaluation by L' is the only trace of it.

Charged against theorem clause (4) as literally stated, not against Step 5, which is correct. Clause (4) instead writes 'Conf_6 -> (reduced-support open of the failure model)'. Since Conf_6 is defined in the same sentence as the full stack of ordered pairwise-distinct sections, that map does not exist; only the base change Conf_6 x_{Div^6} Z^{bal,red} maps to the failure model. As written, clause (4) asserts a torsor structure on a morphism that is not defined. Nothing in the argument establishes that. Charged against theorem clause (5), which carries status 'proved'. (a) The whole justification is Step 6's two sentences: 'The balanced locus is open in the tetragonal locus. The natural map ... is therefore a monomorphism onto the balanced open piece.' The 'therefore' is a non sequitur: openness of a splitting-type stratum in the tetragonal locus has no bearing on injectivity of a map that FORGETS the tetragonal structure gamma. (b) The forgetting is exactly the problem. The source remembers gamma; M_{6,6} does not. A general smooth genus-6 curve carries five distinct g^1_4's (Castelnuovo number rho(6,1,4)=0 with count 5; classically the five conic pencils on the quintic del Pezzo surface containing the canonical model), so the underlying forgetful map is generically 5-to-1 and is emphatically not a monomorphism. What could rescue clause (5) is the incidence condition itself: over a point of M_{6,6} the fibre is {balanced gamma : L_gamma ≅ O_C(Gamma)}, so the mono reduces to recovering the pencil from L. The only standard route is L = omega_C(-D) with D in the pencil, whence |omega_C ⊗ L^{-1}| recovers the pencil — but that is precisely the identification W_5 ≅ omega_C^2(-D) which the attempt explicitly disclaims in Step 8 ('No undischarged identification W_5 ≅ omega_C^2(-D) is used (FND-0073)'). The attempt has therefore removed its own only route to its own clause (5). (c) Monomorphism of stacks is full faithfulness and constrains automorphism groups and T-points, not just geometric points; no automorphism or stack-versus-coarse analysis appears anywhere, and generic injectivity would not suffice in any case. (d) The source of the map is unidentified: Z^{bal}_{ev} ⊂ Div^6 consists of unordered, possibly non-reduced divisors and admits no natural map to M_{6,6} at all. (e) The target is undefined: 'the CE evaluation-failure locus in M_{6,6}' is a condition on a pair (C, gamma), and since every genus-6 curve carries several g^1_4's, this locus is not well-defined on M_{6,6} without saying how gamma is quantified. FND-0091, the only citation offered, warns against the isomorphism claim and presupposes a monomorphism; it does not establish one.

finding_candidates.statement: For (g,n)=(6,6), any claim that the balanced CE failure model maps monomorphically into an evaluation-failure locus in M_{6,6} is equivalent to recovering the tetragonal pencil gamma from the degree-6 bundle L = W_5 ⊗ omega_C^{-1}, because M_{6,6} forgets gamma while a general genus-6 curve carries five distinct g^1_4's, so the underlying forgetful map is generically 5-to-1. Openness of the balanced splitting stratum inside the tetragonal locus is irrelevant to this and supplies no injectivity. The only standard recovery route is the identification L ≅ omega_C(-D) with D in the pencil (equivalently W_5 ≅ omega_C^2(-D)), which returns the pencil as |omega_C ⊗ L^{-1}|; an attempt that disclaims that identification has no remaining route to the monomorphism. Any mono claim additionally needs a well-defined source (the unordered, possibly non-reduced Div^6 model has no map to M_{6,6}), a well-defined target (CE failure is a condition on the pair (C,gamma), not on a point of M_{6,6}), and a stack-level full-faithfulness argument covering automorphism groups.

finding_candidates.statement: In the filtered CE reduction 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0, exactness of pi_* is NOT supplied by finiteness of Gamma over the base. Finiteness of Gamma gives only exactness of restriction to Gamma (the sequence is locally split, so it survives ⊗ O_Gamma) and exactness of pushforward along Gamma -> B. Exactness of pi_* along the curve fibration, i.e. surjectivity of pi_*W -> pi_*W_5, requires R^1 pi_* W_4 = 0, which for (g,n)=(6,6) holds because deg W_4 = 4g+12-16 = 20 > 2g-2 = 10. Likewise coker(phi_4) = 0 requires H^1(W_4(-Gamma)) = 0, i.e. deg 14 > 10, plus commutation of the cokernel with base change and Nakayama to descend from geometric fibres to the sheaf. With those two vanishings the snake lemma and Fit_0(coker phi) = Fit_0(coker phi_5) are correct. Downstream filtered-CE arguments must cite the degree vanishings explicitly, and must recheck them for any (g,n) where deg W_4 <= 2g-2.

finding_candidates.statement: The base-relative Fitting/Abel–Jacobi comparison demanded for C66-GEO-Z separates into a formal part and a genuinely non-formal part, and only the second deserves a gap marker. Formal: with b: Div^n -> Pic^0 the twisted Abel–Jacobi morphism Gamma |-> L(-Gamma), one has coker(phi_5) = R^1 pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)) once R^1 pi_* W_5 = 0, and R^1 pi_* commutes with arbitrary base change in relative dimension 1 while Fit_0 commutes with arbitrary base change and is unchanged by tensoring the module with an invertible sheaf from the base; hence Fit_0(coker phi_5) is the pullback of the Pic^0 answer along b, with no cohomology-and-base-change hypotheses and no constancy of h^0 required — so jumping of h^0(L) and positive-dimensional Abel–Jacobi fibres are harmless here. Non-formal: existence of a Poincare bundle for a universal curve with no section over an algebraic stack base, which exists a priori only up to a G_m-gerbe / Brauer twist, plus a declared scheme structure on the Abel–Jacobi incidence locus. Consequence: an attempt that defines the incidence locus as the scheme-theoretic fibre b^{-1}(e) obtains the scheme-level identification nearly formally, and should say so rather than present it as a substantive theorem; an attempt that leaves the incidence locus' scheme structure undefined has asserted nothing checkable.

The determinantal computation appears to extend to finite flat Gamma (the counts h^0 = g+n-1, kernel H^0(omega) of dimension g, cokernel H^1(omega) of dimension 1, and the perfect Serre pairing as intrinsic derivative do not use etaleness), so the natural repair is to re-adjudicate FND-0096 with 'finite flat' in place of 'finite etale'; until that is done, citations of FND-0096 over a full divisor space should be treated as scoped to the reduced-support open.

strongest_attack: Strongest attack: clause (5), the monomorphism into CE evaluation-failure in M_{6,6} — the only clause that connects the balanced model to the campaign target at all — is marked 'proved' on a non sequitur, and the attempt has disclaimed its own only route to proving it. Step 6's entire argument is that the balanced locus is open in the tetragonal locus, 'therefore' the map is a monomorphism. But the map forgets the tetragonal structure gamma, and openness of a splitting-type stratum says nothing about injectivity of a forgetful map. Concretely: a general smooth genus-6 curve carries five distinct g^1_4's (Castelnuovo count for rho(6,1,4)=0; classically the five conic pencils on the quintic del Pezzo containing the canonical model), so the underlying map {(C,gamma)} -> M_6 is generically 5-to-1 and is not a monomorphism. Injectivity can only come from the incidence condition pinning down gamma: the fibre over a point of M_{6,6} is {balanced gamma : L_gamma ≅ O_C(Gamma)}, so clause (5) is equivalent to recovering the pencil from the degree-6 bundle L. The one standard way to do that is L = omega_C(-D) with D in the pencil, so that |omega_C ⊗ L^{-1}| returns the pencil — and that is exactly the identification W_5 ≅ omega_C^2(-D) which Step 8 explicitly disclaims as undischarged. The attempt therefore asserts as proved a statement whose only known proof it has removed from scope. This is compounded by clause (5) having neither a well-defined source (Z^{bal}_{ev} consists of unordered, possibly non-reduced divisors and admits no natural map to M_{6,6}) nor a well-defined target (CE evaluation-failure is a condition on a pair (C,gamma), so it is not a locus in M_{6,6} until gamma is quantified), and by monomorphism of stacks being a full-faithfulness condition on which no automorphism analysis is offered. Runner-up attack, and the reason the verdict is incomplete rather than refuted: clause (3) faces an unaddressed dilemma. Z^{bal}_{AJ} is never given a scheme structure, so 'equals as closed subschemes' has no determinate meaning; if Z^{bal}_{AJ} is defined as the scheme-theoretic fibre b^{-1}(e) of the twisted Abel–Jacobi morphism, the clause follows nearly formally from FND-0096 plus the standard facts that Fit_0 and R^1pi_* both commute with arbitrary base change in relative dimension 1, and carries far less content than advertised; otherwise it is unproved — and either way it is asserted flatly while the supporting claim is self-declared 'gap' at high severity. theorem_statement: Let B^{bal} be the moduli stack of smooth genus-6 balanced tetragonal curves (degree-4 covers gamma: C -> P^1 with fibrewise F ≅ O(4) ⊕ O(5)). Let 0 → L_5 → F → L_4 → 0 be the relative Harder–Narasimhan filtration of F, and let 0 → W_4 → W → W_5 → 0 be the induced canonical filtration of the Casnati–Ekedahl bundle, with W_5 := (O_{P(E^vee)}(2) ⊗ gamma^* O_{P^1}(-5))|_C the degree-16 quotient (not the O(5) summand of F) and L := W_5 ⊗ omega_{C/B^{bal}}^{-1} of fibrewise degree 6. Let Div^6_{C/B} be the relative effective-divisor space of degree 6, phi (resp. phi_5) the relative CE evaluation map for W|_Gamma (resp. W_5|_Gamma), and Conf_6 the stack of ordered pairwise-distinct sections. Define Z^{bal}_{ev} := V(Fit_0(coker phi)) ⊂ Div^6_{C/B} and Z^{bal}_{AJ} the Abel–Jacobi incidence of O_C(Gamma) ≅ L. Then: (1) Fit_0(coker phi) = Fit_0(coker phi_5) with no global split of W used; (2) on geometric balanced fibres, CE evaluation fails on effective deg-6 Gamma iff O_C(Gamma) ≅ L; (3) scheme-theoretically, Z^{bal}_{ev} is cut out by Fit_0(coker phi_5), and equals Z^{bal}_{AJ} after the universal Pic^0 Fitting comparison at the degree-zero CE obstruction (residual base-relative writeup gap recorded); (4) Conf_6 → (reduced-support open of the failure model) is a finite étale S_6-torsor over that open, which is open in the failure model and is not a closed pure-codimension subvariety of M_{6,6}; (5) the natural map of the balanced model into CE evaluation-failure in M_{6,6} is a monomorphism onto the balanced open piece and is not claimed to be an isomorphism onto all CE failure. Explicitly excluded: pure dimension 17, global codimension 4, constant h^0(L)=3 / relative P^2 structure, components/stabilizers/closure analysis, non-closedness of Z^{bal} without a point of Z \ Z^{bal}, Tate type of any cohomology of Z, and construction of unbalanced tetragonal failure.
